Gradual

/GRAD-oo-ul/ — emphasis on first syllable · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Gradual means happening slowly and in small stages rather than all at once.

No flood or earthquake shaped these towering walls; instead, the change was gradual, so slow that no single generation would ever have noticed it.

Worked Example

The patient stopped smoking, and her lung capacity improved month by month—slowly at first, then more noticeably—a gradual recovery that her doctor marked on a chart.

Gradual is more precise than a plain word like 'slow' or 'better' because it emphasizes that the change happens in distinct stages over time, not just slowly.

How Gradual Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

slow

slow: unhurried pace, without implying distinct stages

progressive

progressive: advancing step by step, forward-moving

steady

steady: regular and even, not necessarily slow

Antonyms

sudden

sudden: happening all at once, without warning

instantaneous

instantaneous: finished completely in a single instant

How Strong Is It? — glacial → gradual

glacial vs. gradual

glacial vs. gradual: Progress on the trade treaty was glacial, so slow that it felt like nothing was moving at all; gradual is the better word for the reservoir's rise behind the new dam, because it promises real, measurable advancement in stages rather than mere extreme slowness.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of gradual.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — grad-

Root — grad-: step, degree

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to, of the nature of

Put it together

Put it together: Grad- (step, degree) + -al (relating to) = relating to steps or degrees — happening one small step at a time rather than all at once. There is no prefix hiding here: gradual comes straight from Latin gradus ('a step') plus the adjective ending -alis. The same stepping root walks through grade, graduate, and upgrade.

Use the root in a new word: upgrade

Use the root in a new word: upgrade: The airline decided to upgrade the passengers sitting in coach to first-class seats.

Word Choice

neutral

Gradual describes change that's slow and happens in stages—perfect when you want to show that something advances in noticeable increments. When the slowness matters more than the stages, 'slow' alone is fine.
